732871903.text: Bandits? How rude! I am Mendas, a scout! And this is Hugeweh.

732871904.text: We are adventurers just passing by.

732871905.text: Here... the Matriarch has forbidden us from harming foreign adventurers, you must hurry up and get out of here!

732871906.text: Gah. If only Jeht were here. She's better at dealing with outsiders...

732871908.text: Well, what's the matter, then? She joined us some time back and is highly valued by the Matriarch.

732871909.text: She's practically the Matriarch's shadow... Hmph, none of us tribespeople even come close to that kind of treatment.

732871913.text: Well, if you're Jeht's friends, I won't stop you. You may move on. The tribe's campsite lies ahead.

732871914.text: Jeht isn't back yet, but Aderfi, Masseira, and Yuften are in at the moment. They're pretty friendly to outsiders.

732871915.text: You can look for them... But if you have lied to us, you will find us less merciful.

732872101.text: B—But... I don't know what those outsiders wanted... It's not my fault! Please let me explain, Matriarch Babel...

732872103.text: Please... Please! Give me one more chance, Matriarch... My Lady! I will prove my loyalty to the Tanit... Please believe me... I would gladly offer my life...

732872105.text: She who knocked your teeth out can also remove your tongue.

732872107.text: I don't understand... If you're willing to give your life for the Tanit, why are you still standing before me, alive?

732872108.text: And another thing... Why did you address me as "My Lady"?

732872109.text: I don't speak the language of the snowlands, and I do not care for the sophistry of the so-called "civilized world"... There is no such thing as "My Lady" here.

732872110.text: And do enlighten me. What makes you think I'm not your family anymore... but some "Lady"?

732872111.text: Your tongue is tainted with outsider poison, your mind stained by their gold. You cannot remain here.

732872112.text: I shall speak no further. Lead him away... He was once one of us, so you know what to do.

732872113.text: The weeping man is taken away, leaving an uneasy silence...

732872114.text: After a while, the crowd begins to disperse, making room for you to see the Matriarch.

732872115.text: (Uh, what just happened...? Whatever it was, it sounded scary!)

732872119.text: Ah... My apologies, children. I was a little distracted. I forgot you were there.

732872120.text: I'm terribly sorry that you had to see... that. I'm at fault. As the Matriarch of the Tanit, I'd like to make amends.

732872121.text: Uh, n—no need! Y'know, what with that "teeth and tongue" stuff and all...

732872122.text: Heh... We were simply meting out punishment against a traitor. All the same, I am sorry for having given you such a terrible first impression as Matriarch.

732872123.text: The city has its laws, and the tribe has its rules — please, do not pay it too much mind.

732872124.text: #So you two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon, yes? Jeht talks about you two a lot.

732872126.text: We came to look for Jeht.

732872127.text: This doesn't seem like a good time, though.

732872128.text: Ah, no need to be so polite! Indeed, I should say that you have impeccable timing.

732872129.text: It was I who approved her invitation in the first place. That is how you got safely past the Tanit's hunting grounds.

732872130.text: Hehe. While I do feel bad saying this... I invited you here to help Jeht with some unfinished business.

732872132.text: Don't worry. We weren't trying to hunt you. You are an honored guest here. For so long as we remember our guests' faces, we shall never do them harm on our land.

732872134.text: Haha. Now then, don't let me spoil the fun for you young folks... Look, Jeht is here.

732872136.text: How did it go with that fellow?

732872137.text: I made sure that he was given sufficient dignity.

732872138.text: ...That's good. But do not be proud of this deed, child. This was a tragic affair. He was my tribesman, and yours also.

732872140.text: Haha, alright. This is not a good day to preach. The friends you have been waiting for have finally arrived, so set your tears aside and greet them with joy.

732872143.text: Hey, Jeht! We're here to see you!

732872144.text: #{NICKNAME}! And Paimon, too! You really did come!

732872145.text: Thank you, Matriarch Babel! I shouldn't have gotten mad at everyone about it...

732872146.text: Now, now, of course I'm happy to see you all together. Whatever it is that you want to see or do, I've already approved it. You can put your doubts to rest.

732872147.text: A word of caution, however... The road ahead of you will be fraught with danger and intrigue, so be on your guard. Please stay safe...

732872148.text: Matriarch Babel, Azariq has sent me to deliver a message to you.

732872150.text: If you'll excuse me, I have tribal affairs to attend to. I'll leave you young ones to catch up.

732872152.text: Babel hurries away together with the messenger.

732872153.text: Jeht, you've changed a lot since we last saw you!

732872154.text: Hehe, got a good eye, haven't you, Paimon? So, what's different about me?

732872155.text: You look a little more tanned...

subQuests.subQuestName: Katheryne seems to be looking for you...

732870101.text: Hello there. We have a letter for you — it's from Ms. Jeht.

732870102.text: Eh? So you know Jeht, too, Katheryne? How's she doing?

732870103.text: The Adventurers' Guild has an open partnership with the Eremites, so it would be more surprising if I didn't know her. She looked quite happy when she arrived, and said she was looking forward to seeing you again.

732870105.text: Well... Looks like she's having a good time. Better than the last time we saw each other!

732870106.text: But, what's this? "The Tanit camp"? That name sorta rings a bell. Have we been there before?

732870107.text: The Tanit are the tribe from which Jeht hails. Their campsite is in the depths of Deshret Desert, amidst the ruins of what was once the city of Gurabad. If you don't mind, I'll mark it out on your map.

732870108.text: Wow... Katheryne really is a walking, breathing encyclopedia...

732870111.text: #You flatter me, {NICKNAME}. In order to better serve adventurers, it is the duty of the Adventurers' Guild to provide such basic information whenever it is needed.

732870112.text: And the Tanit have always had good commercial relations with the Adventurers' Guild. With Ms. Jeht as our point of contact, they have proven themselves reliable across many acts of cooperation.

732870113.text: Well... The letter also says that she'd like to settle some unfinished business and has expressly asked us to come along. How mysterious... did she mention anything specific, Katheryne?

732870114.text: Well, I'm not at liberty to infringe upon the sender's privacy. I'm afraid the only way you'll find out is if you pay her a visit in person.

732870115.text: So, there's information that even you can't get a hold of, huh?

732870116.text: Sorry. This isn't a matter of ability or lack thereof, but a matter of professionalism. We do not accept any complaints on this front.

732870117.text: The Tanit campsite has been marked on your map for you. They'll be settling there for the next two or three years, as is the custom of tribal migration.

732870118.text: If they happen to not be at this location, please do not hesitate to contact me. I will update you concerning their migratory pattern as soon as possible.

732870119.text: Uh, that's real thoughtful of you, but Paimon doesn't think we're gonna wait two to three years to go look for Jeht...

732870120.text: #Okay, {NICKNAME}. Now that we know where Jeht is, what are we waiting for? Let's not keep her waiting!

732870121.text: In that case, do contact her for more specific information... Oh, sorry. I forgot to mention that this is not a guild commission. It should just be a meeting between friends...

732870122.text: Anyway, ad astra abyssosque! May your reunion lead to new happy encounters and adventures!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Tanit tribe and find Jeht

732870403.text: Bandits? How rude! I am Mendas, a scout! And this is Hugeweh.

732870405.text: Yes! Jeht sent us a letter, and that's why we're here!

732870407.text: You give Jeht's letter to the scout for review...

732870408.text: Well, if you're Jeht's friends, I won't stop you. You may move on. The tribe's campsite lies ahead.

732870409.text: Jeht isn't back yet, but Aderfi, Masseira, and Yuften are in at the moment. They're pretty friendly to outsiders.

732870410.text: Don't hesitate to seek them out... But if you dare deceive us, you will find us quite unfriendly indeed.

732871801.text: Hello, young ones. What do you need?

732871802.text: Well... We're here to see Jeht. Is she around?

732871803.text: Jeht? Yes... she's here. Why are you looking for her?

732871806.text: #She's mentioned you before, I think. Something about a "brave and reliable {M#young man}{F#young woman}." Hmph, she's been hanging around outside for too long, I see, to be making friends with rich people in fancy clothing and such.

732871808.text: Hey, what's that supposed to mean!?

732871809.text: Sorry for speaking so rudely, but I care little for receiving outsiders. You should seek out Matriarch Babel instead.

732871813.text: What do you mean "so"? She's a good kid. I don't want to see her come under the bad influence of outsiders. Like I said before, if you need anything, seek out Matriarch Babel. Don't bother me.

732871816.text: Well, I have nothing much else to say to you... Why don't you go find Masseira? He's a strange old man. Who knows, maybe you'll get a warmer welcome there.

732871815.text: What do I do? I do business, exchanging our trash for trash from the city.

732871704.text: Shh... Let me guess... You're here to find someone. Your friend, yes?

732871706.text: Jeht is a good girl. I'm glad she has a friend like you.

732871708.text: Hehe. Anyway, if you don't mind a little advice... You look like a real killer, that you do. But "companions"? Those will prove to be your undoing... Your fatal weakness.

732871709.text: I don't understand what you're trying to say...

732871710.text: Then consider my words but a breeze in your ear. Hmm... Matriarch Babel's not back yet, so you can go talk to Yuften. He's right by the creek where we raise crocodiles. You can't miss it.

732870501.text: Hello, stranger. What d—do you need?

732870503.text: Oh, the M—Matriarch told me about you. You're good folk.

732870508.text: If you're looking for Jeht, sh—she's still out... Please go to meet Matriarch Babel first. She has b—been waiting for you for a long time.

732870512.text: She's made friends, is very happy, and talks like a l—l—little antelope... I'm very... very happy for her.

732870513.text: Hmm, it's getting busy up there. Matriarch Babel has returned. O—okay, you should probably meet her. Please don't keep her w—waiting too long.

732870505.text: Huh? I d—don't need... Why are you asking?

732870506.text: Oh, you mean the way I t—talk, right?

732870507.text: Haha... I'm used t—to it, and I hope you will be, too. Speaking a little slower makes your train of th—thought all the clearer.

732870701.text: B—But... I don't know what those outsiders wanted... It's not my fault! Please let me explain, Matriarch Babel...

732870703.text: Please... Please! Give me one more chance, Matriarch... My Lady! I will prove my loyalty to the Tanit... Please believe me... I would gladly offer my life...

732870705.text: She who knocked your teeth out can also remove your tongue.

732870707.text: I don't understand... If you're willing to give your life for the Tanit, why are you still standing before me, alive?

732870708.text: And another thing... Why did you address me as "My Lady"?

732870709.text: I don't speak the language of the snowlands, and I do not care for the sophistry of the so-called "civilized world"... There is no such thing as "My Lady" here.

732870710.text: And do enlighten me. What makes you think I'm not your family anymore... but some "Lady"?

732870711.text: Your tongue is tainted with outsider poison, your mind stained by their gold. You cannot remain here.

732870712.text: I shall speak no further. Lead him away... He was once one of us, so you know what to do.

732870713.text: The weeping man is taken away, leaving an uneasy silence...

732870714.text: After a while, the crowd begins to disperse, making room for you to see the Matriarch.

732870715.text: (Uh, what just happened...? Whatever it was, it sounded scary!)

732870719.text: Ah... My apologies, children. I was a little distracted. I forgot you were there.

732870720.text: I'm terribly sorry that you had to see... that. I'm at fault. As the Matriarch of the Tanit, I'd like to make amends.

732870721.text: Uh, n—no need! Y'know, what with that "teeth and tongue" stuff and all...

732870722.text: Heh... We were simply meting out punishment against a traitor. All the same, I am sorry for having given you such a terrible first impression as Matriarch.

732870723.text: The city has its laws, and the tribe has its rules — please, do not pay it too much mind.

732870724.text: #So you two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon, yes? Jeht talks about you two a lot.

732870801.text: #I'm here, Yuften! And I've brought my friends, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

732870802.text: H—Hello, Jeht. Have you finished your b—b—business?

732870803.text: Yep, and that's why I thought I should come here to help you out, and brought my friends along to boot!

732870804.text: Oh? Thank you, Jeht. You r—r—remembered that I had something I needed your help with!

732870805.text: Haha. Back when Elder Bleda was around, you used to pester him to f—f—feed the crocodiles together with you...

732870807.text: Um, alright... Here's the f—f—food. The meat's fresh. Take it.

subQuests.subQuestName: Feed the crocodiles together with Jeht

732871001.text: Feeding crocodiles is pretty easy... You drop the meat, they follow the scent, and they eat it themselves.

732871002.text: By the way, your Matriarch seems pretty fearsome...

732871003.text: Oh, you mean what happened just now? Well, it's nothing. We were just dealing with a traitor.

732871004.text: I tracked him through the desert for half a month before bringing him back alive. He was crafty, and plenty fierce to boot. I had to knock some of his teeth out to subdue him... Argh, my hand still hurts...

732871006.text: So be careful what you say around me in the future, eh, Paimon?

732871010.text: Hahaha, don't be so serious! We're all friends here. I'm just kidding!

subQuests.subQuestName: Feed the crocodiles together with Jeht

732871201.text: It does look like you're taken seriously around here... Everyone seems to respect you!

732871202.text: Well, here's the thing... Because of my previous experience with adventurers, I'm more perceptive about things that happen outside the tribe.

732871203.text: So the Matriarch decided that it would be my job to track down outsiders and punish traitors to the tribe.

732871206.text: Since I wasn't born amongst the Tanit, it's okay for me to deal with criminals in a more aggressive way... That's what Matriarch Babel told me.

732871207.text: Although I don't really care... I'm not sure if this is a special privilege or proof of our estrangement.

732871208.text: Well, I wasn't born here, after all, and the Tanit tribe isn't a home I'm innately familiar with. I can only try my best to do everything well. As long as I can put some roots down, I think I'll be fine.

732871302.text: Yeah. I'm going to wash now! Your crocodile food stinks — smells of raw meat!

732871303.text: Haha... And d—does that or traitor-blood smell worse?

732871305.text: Thank you. By the way... th—there's one more thing that I want to a—ask of you...

732871306.text: This is the cured c—c—crocodile meat that I promised to give Aderfi previously. Pass it on to him for me, would you?

732871307.text: Sure, sure, I'll give your c—c—crocodile meat to Aderfi, no problem!

732871402.text: Oh? Here to show off your new outsider friends?

732871403.text: Sort of! By the way, here's the crocodile jerky from Yuften!

732871405.text: Hehe, no worries! By the way, about Benben... can you still fix it?

732871406.text: Don't worry, it's nothing serious. I'll be able to get it back to you in a couple of days.

732871407.text: Oh... okay! Then I'll get going!

732871601.text: Heh... running here and there really works up a sweat...

732871604.text: Haha, it's fine. I don't like being idle, actually.

732871605.text: Ah, but look at me. I didn't invite you guys here so you could come run errands with me!

732871606.text: Well, so here's the story: Matriarch Babel recently agreed to let me bring Dad's... my father's remains, and those of my mother, to be buried in the Eternal Oasis.

732871607.text: Oh? So that's a real place? Paimon thought that it was just a myth.

732871608.text: Well, the last time we parted, I was so lost... I honestly didn't know where to start looking for it. Matriarch Babel, however, seems very sure that the Eternal Oasis lies in the middle of this desert...

732871609.text: The Tanit tribe holds that the never-ending sandstorm at the heart of the desert conceals the Eternal Oasis.

732871610.text: Unfortunately, that area has been sealed off by the tribe as a taboo place. No one can approach except scouts on patrol.

732871611.text: Taboo...? Is it dangerous or something?

732871612.text: Yes. Some older folks believe that ancient spirits roam there, hungering for souls and flesh... But that's probably just a myth. I don't believe it.

732873101.text: Well? Are you ready to go?

732873105.text: Be my guest. If you need anything, come to me anytime!

732873201.text: Alright, alright. I've got my work to do, and you've got yours. There's no need to look around here anymore.

732873301.text: If you need to see Jeht, you'll have to wait for Matriarch Babel... Why, you ask? Well, you'll see...

732873401.text: G—Go see the Matriarch. I'm sure she and Jeht will be very h—happy to see you.

732873502.text: You've already met the Matriarch? If you haven't gotten kicked out, that means you're our honored guest... Well, feel free to wander as you like, then.

732873504.text: Hmm? You've got a good eye, I must say. Yes, I am indeed a merchant. I sell the various things that the tribe lacks. Cosmetics, luxury items, costumes, toys, agricultural products, intricate tools...

732873505.text: What would you like? If you should need something, I'll have it. And if I don't, just tell me what you need, and I'll get it for you, whether it's from the city, or even from Fontaine!

732873506.text: Ah... Right, you're an outsider. Well, in that case, you have my apologies, but my shop is not open to you.

732873507.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

732873513.text: You've got lots of books here. May I read them?

732873514.text: The books? Oh! Right, those are here at the request of Matriarch Babel. I'm sure you've heard, and seen, that the city people have taken to using this thing called the Akasha, which they mount on their ears.

732873515.text: Their libraries have been emptied of a great number of obsolete books, and the Matriarch had me purchase and safe-keep them for everyone to read free of charge. Hmph... I operated at a loss there.

732873516.text: As for the Akasha, we did ship a set in from another tribe, but it was... very inconvenient to use, not to mention quite arcane indeed. We could not disassemble or repair it, for the wiring was too centralized...

732873517.text: Whatever the case, I'd say that reading books on your own is far better than relying on some strange machine to stuff information into your brain.

732873518.text: After all, who knows what back doors you might open if you just let people into the door of your mind?

732873520.text: Don't let me get in your way.

732873509.text: Straight to the point, hmm? I like buyers like you. Unfortunately, I don't sell to outsiders.

732873510.text: Um, this is not due to xenophobia or some kind of base prejudice. It's more that... Our tribe and the merchants in the cities don't share economic spheres, if you can glean my meaning?

732873511.text: I only serve the Tanit tribe, you know, as our exclusive distributer of goods. All trade and other transactions have to go through Matriarch Babel, and I take a small cut of that.

732873512.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

732873601.text: Spoken to Babel, have you? Ah, she's probably busying herself somewhere else again... You would sooner stop the wind than stop her.

732873602.text: Haha... You know, youngster, speaking of the wind... I'd like to remind you of a kind of desert wind that we call "Zibri."

732873603.text: At first, you won't sense anything, until the sandstorm rises over the horizon, and the air itself begins to ascend and burn. Only then will you realize...

732873604.text: ...That you can no longer smell anything, for the heated air has smothered your sense of smell, seared your nostrils...

732873605.text: By then... Heh. By then, it will be too late.

732873606.text: I'm afraid I didn't catch your drift...

732873607.text: It's nothing... I just mean to say that you should be careful of the sandstorms.

732873701.text: Those crocodiles are a v—very gentle... Still, be careful when you feed them...

732873802.text: Matriarch Babel mentioned you previously, honored guest. Please, have a look around.

732873804.text: Hmm...? I thought I had already introduced myself... I sell the various things that the tribe lacks. Cosmetics, luxury items, costumes, toys, agricultural products, intricate tools...

732873805.text: What would you like? If you should need something, I'll have it. And if I don't, just tell me what you need, and I'll get it for you, whether it's from the city, or even from Fontaine!

732873806.text: Ah... Right, you're an outsider. Well, in that case, you have my apologies, but my shop is not open to you.

732873807.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

732873819.text: You've got lots of books here. May I read them?

732873820.text: Books? ...Oh, right, you mean the ones Matriarch Babel requested... See, it's been fashionable for city people to wear Akasha on their ears for some time. You must have seen them.

732873821.text: Their libraries have been emptied of a great number of obsolete books, and the Matriarch had me purchase and safe-keep them for everyone to read free of charge. Hmph... I operated at a loss there.

732873822.text: As for the Akasha, we did ship a set in from another tribe, but it was... very inconvenient to use, not to mention quite arcane indeed. We could not disassemble or repair it, for the wiring was too centralized...

732873823.text: Whatever the case, I'd say that reading books on your own is far better than relying on some strange machine to stuff information into your brain.

732873824.text: After all, who knows what back doors you might open if you just let people into the door of your mind?

732873826.text: Don't let me get in your way.

732873809.text: Straight to the point, hmm? I like buyers like you. Unfortunately, I don't sell to outsiders.

732873810.text: Um, this is not due to xenophobia or some kind of base prejudice. It's more that... Our tribe and the merchants in the cities don't share economic spheres, if you can glean my meaning?

732873811.text: I only serve the Tanit tribe, you know, as our exclusive distributer of goods. All trade and other transactions have to go through Matriarch Babel, and I take a small cut of that.

732873812.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

732873814.text: Benben... Ah, you mean the little machine that follows Jeht around.

732873815.text: I've examined it before. There's nothing particularly wrong with it, but as for how it can be restored to its former, energetic state...

732873816.text: I have my ways... but I don't think I could tell you.

732873817.text: Whatever the case, I think it's best that it stays with me till the repairs are done.

732873818.text: Anything else you'd like to ask me?

732873902.text: J—J—Jeht mentions you often. She's a good kid.

732873904.text: Planting crops and f—feeding the fish. Sometimes, I also do some b—b—butchery. Crocodile skin and meat is v—very useful.

732873908.text: We get clean spring water all year around h—here, so it's just right for raising crocodiles. Th—that's why we fenced this place up.

732873909.text: Crocodiles are easy to care for, and they can be harvested for lots of skins and meat. Unfortunately, f—fields are a d—different story...

732873911.text: We do... but only for testing. Matriarch Babel invited some outsiders to c—c—come and provide us with Anahitian Blessing, and she got all these old books from the city...

732873912.text: S—s—so we've tried our hand at farming according to the contents of these books.

732873913.text: But the oases in the canyon are too narrow and lack nutrients. We need to find a way to f—fertilize the soil.

732873914.text: Tell me about the Anahitian Blessing...

732873915.text: The outsiders didn't want to reveal the fertilizer's composition. As such, we've had to rely on the people who provide it to f—fertilize the soil... which isn't good.

732873916.text: Th—that's why the Matriarch wants me to d—do some research here to r—reverse engineer our own Anahitian Blessing.

732873917.text: I shan't disturb you any longer.

732873918.text: Th—that's alright. Please take some crocodile jerky, dear guest. It's just over there...

732873906.text: Hehe, yes. I—I take care of them. These are quite large and obedient...

732873907.text: This one's c—c—called Sedim. Very fierce and strong, and skin's very vibrant. It'll make for a good satchel. And there's that one, Karam. It's small but plump. Rather gentle, too.

732879901.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME}! If it's convenient, there's a message for you here!

732879907.text: Come with me. Don't let the crocodiles bite your foot!

732879909.text: Unlike in the rainforest, the crocodiles here are docile and much smaller.

732879910.text: They've sacrificed a lot to adapt to living in the desert.

732879914.text: Aderfi has a lot of nice stuff that you can't find or trade, and people like to go there to do business.

732879915.text: Y'know, to get things like... gadgets, toys, new clothes... and cosmetics...

732879917.text: What do you even mean by that? Lapis lazuli eye shadow is an essential sunscreen for us desert folk, and we can use concealer to hide scars. Makeup's super useful!

732879919.text: You arrive at a canyon, but your path has been barred...

732879920.text: Hehe... It's good that you were able to come.

732879921.text: We're glad to see you too, Jeht! There's so much we'd like to tell you, but... Hmm, where should we even begin?

732879922.text: I know, right? There's so much we all want to say, but now that we've met... Hehe, "where should we start," huh?

732879923.text: I've learned a phrase here in the tribe, and it goes something like "the closer your home, the more reticent your heart." And, y'know, it describes our situation perfectly.

732879924.text: Whoa, is this tribe always so... er, eloquent?
